'''Vladimir Aleksandrovich Teplyakov''' ({{langx|ru|Владимир Александрович Тепляков}}) (6 November 1925 – 10 December 2009) was a [[List of Russian inventors|Russian experimental physicist]] known for his work on [[particle accelerator]]s. Together with I.M. Kapchinsky, he invented the principle of the [[radio-frequency quadrupole]] (RFQ), which revolutionized the acceleration of low-energy [[charged particle beam]]s.<ref name="IFMIF">{{cite web| author = E H Shibuya| title = RFQ pioneer celebrates 80th birthday| publisher = Cern Courier| date = 2 November 2005| url = http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29474/3| access-date = 14 December 2009| archive-date = 20 February 2012| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120220105025/http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/29474/3| url-status = dead}}</ref>

==Biography==
Teplyakov was born in [[Tambov]], [[Russia]]. At the age of 17, in January 1943, he was drafted into the [[Red Army]] to fight in the [[World War II|Second World War]], serving in the [[3rd Ukrainian Front]]. He participated in a number of operations in [[Right-bank Ukraine]], [[Moldavia]] and [[Eastern Europe]] and was awarded combat orders and medals.<ref>{{cite web|author1=Jan Cherniak |author2=Jane Zavalishina |author3=Elena Kolmanovskaya |author4=Ekaterina Solntseva |title=List of Veterans in the Moscow Area| year = 2005 | url = http://www.pobediteli.ru/russia/center/moskovskaya/t/tek-tib/index.html| access-date = 14 December 2009}}</ref>

After the war, he graduated from the All-Union Correspondence Polytechnic Institute in [[Moscow]] and joined the team of scientists at the [[Semenov Institute of Chemical Physics|Institute of Chemical Physics]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences|Soviet Academy of Sciences]] who worked on the large particle accelerator for conversion of [[uranium-238]] into [[weapons-grade]] [[plutonium-239]].<ref name=Protvinonews>[http://www.protvino.ru/news/121/ ''"Vladimir Teplyakov"''] Retrieved on 12 December 2009</ref> From 1959 to 1966 he worked at [[Snezhinsk|Chelyabinsk-70]] to develop a high-current proton [[linear particle accelerator]] ("linac") for controlled [[thermonuclear fusion]]. In the mid-1960s, together with G. M. Anisimov, Teplyakov conceived the idea of focusing the charged particle beams by the radio-frequency (RF) accelerating electromagnetic field rather than by solenoid magnets. This work continued at the [[Institute for High Energy Physics]] (IHEP) in [[Protvino]], where his group moved in 1966 to build the I-100, a 100 MeV Alvarez drift-tube linac, which was an injector to the [[U-70 (synchrotron)|U-70]], a 70 GeV proton [[synchrotron]], the world's largest particle accelerator at that time.<ref name=IFMIF/><ref>{{cite web|title=Vladimir Aleksandrovich Teplyakov, Translation from Atomnaya Energiya, Vol. 99| date = 5 November 2005 | url = http://resources.metapress.com/pdf-preview.axd?code=a66375864pp587wm&size=largest| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110714080353/http://resources.metapress.com/pdf-preview.axd?code=a66375864pp587wm&size=largest| url-status = usurped| archive-date = 14 July 2011| access-date = 14 December 2009}}</ref>

By the late 1960s, Teplyakov and I. M. Kapchinsky developed the concept of the [[radio-frequency quadrupole]] (RFQ), where accelerating gaps are supplemented with spacer electrodes charged under an intermediate potential. Such a focusing system resulted in a noticeable upgrade in performance and a significant decrease in the dimensions of the drift tubes. Teplyakov subsequently developed several RFQ drift-tube structures and RF cavities to drive them.<ref name=IFMIF/><ref>{{cite web|author=Yu. Budanov|title=Accelerator Application to Medicine and Technology|url=http://accelconf.web.cern.ch/AccelConf/r08/html/authors/521.htm|access-date=14 December 2009|archive-date=17 November 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117212432/http://accelconf.web.cern.ch/ACCELCONF/r08/html/authors/521.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=T. M. Kapchinskij|author2=N. V. Lazarev|title=The Linear Accelerator Structures with Space-uniform Quadrupole Focusing|journal=IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science|volume=NS-26|issue=3|url=http://accelconf.web.cern.ch/AccelConf/p79/PDF/PAC1979_3462.PDF|access-date=14 December 2009|archive-date=18 November 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101118045654/http://accelconf.web.cern.ch/ACCELCONF/p79/PDF/PAC1979_3462.PDF|url-status=dead}}</ref> The URAL-30 proton linac was commissioned in 1977. It applies a through front-to-end RFQ-focusing up to the top energy of 30 MeV. Since 1985 URAL-30 routinely operates as an injector to the booster proton synchrotron of IHEP.<ref>{{cite web|author=Yu. Budanov|url=https://accelconf.web.cern.ch/accelconf/r06/PAPERS/MOEP02.PDF|title=Status of the Ural-30M Linac — A Novel Injector to the Accelerator Complex of IHEP|collaboration=O. Belyaev, I. Zvonarev, A. Maltsev, E. Mazurov, V. Stephanov, S. Strekalovskyh, V. Teplyakov, N. Tyurin|work=Proceedings of RuPAC 2006, Novosibirsk, Russia|access-date=8 May 2017}}</ref>

Teplyakov was the author of more than 100 inventions and scientific papers, and was the co-author of the book ''Linear Accelerators of Ions''.<ref name=Protvinonews/><ref>D.V. Karetnikov, I.Kh. Slivkov, V.Y. Teplyakov ''et al.'' "Линейные ускорители ионов" (Linear Accelerators of Ions). Moscow, Госатомиздат, 1962, 208 pp. (in Russian)</ref>

==Honours and awards==
For the invention of the RFQ, Teplyakov was awarded the 1988 [[Lenin Prize]] (together with Kapchinsky) and the U.S. Particle Accelerator School Prize for Achievement in Accelerator Physics and Technology.<ref name=IFMIF/><ref>[http://www.ihep.su/ihep/discovery/prize_lst.htm ''"Циклы научных работ, выполненные в ГНЦ ИФВЭ и удостоенные высших государственных премий" (Scientific work made in IHEP and awarded the highest state awards)''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306203406/http://www.ihep.su/ihep/discovery/prize_lst.htm |date=6 March 2016 }} Retrieved on 11 December 2009</ref> In 2006, the European Physical Society awarded him the prize "[[Rolf Wideroe Prize|for outstanding work in the accelerator field]]".<ref>[http://epac.web.cern.ch/EPAC/EPS-AG/Accelerator_Prizes/EPS-AG_Prize_Winners.htm ''"Recipients of EPS-AG Accelerator Prizes"''] Retrieved on 12 December 2009</ref> Teplyakov received the highest decorations bestowed by the Soviet Union, the [[Order of Lenin]] and the [[Order of the October Revolution]].<ref name="ScienceObituary">{{cite web|url=http://www.za-nauku.ru/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=2363&Itemid=39|title=In Memory of the Scientist Vladimir Alexandrovich Teplyakov|date=16 December 2009|publisher=Trade Union Committee of the IHEP|language=ru|access-date=8 May 2017}}</ref> He was one of the first to receive the title "Veteran of Nuclear Industry" and also received the title "Honored Worker of Science and Technology of the Russian Federation".<ref>{{cite press release|title=Presidential Decree On awarding state awards of the Russian Federation to workers of joint-stock companies, enterprises and organizations|publisher=President Boris Yeltsin|date=18 October 1995|language=ru|url=http://pravo.gov.ru/proxy/ips/?doc_itself=&&nd=102037730&&page=1&rdk=0#I0|access-date=8 May 2017}}</ref> Teplyakov died on 10 December 2009.<ref name="ScienceObituary" />
